name: Construction
blurb: Computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning, sourced from AGC, BuiltWorlds, and the proptech and contech trackers.

points.desc: The Census BTOS series reports construction AI use directly from firms, fortnightly.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The construction-technology research network tracks site robotics, jobsite IoT, and digital preconstruction across research programs and member benchmarking.
points.name: BuiltWorlds runs the sector intelligence

points.desc: The Associated General Contractors of America surveys technology adoption and safety-technology compliance across US builders - the trade body's data is the adoption record.
points.name: AGC tracks contractor adoption

points.desc: CREtech and MetaProp track venture flow across architecture, engineering, and construction technology alongside property tech.
points.name: Proptech capital reaches AEC too

summary: Computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning are the working deployments - the sector's AI mostly watches the jobsite and checks the model against reality before concrete is poured.

analysis.body:
Construction firms reported AI use at 14.9% in the most recent Census Business Trends and Outlook Survey period, up from 13.6% the prior period, placing the sector in the measured middle of the economy rather than at either extreme. The increase is modest but consistent with a trade where procurement cycles are long, project-by-project contracting complicates firm-level technology decisions, and jobsite conditions are inherently variable. The Census series asks only whether AI was used in the preceding two weeks, so the figure captures active deployment rather than aspiration.

The documented applications concentrate in three areas: computer-vision safety monitoring, Building Information Modeling clash detection during preconstruction, and autonomous site scanning. Safety monitoring uses cameras and inference models to flag hazards such as missing personal protective equipment or workers entering restricted zones, which addresses one of construction's most persistent liability and regulatory exposures. BIM clash detection applies AI to identify conflicts between structural, mechanical, and electrical models before work begins, reducing costly rework. Autonomous scanning tools, often mounted on robots or drones, generate as-built records that can be compared against design intent throughout a project.

The organizations tracking this most closely are the Associated General Contractors of America on the contractor adoption and safety-compliance side, and BuiltWorlds on the broader site robotics and jobsite IoT research side. Venture capital flow into construction technology is monitored by CREtech and MetaProp alongside the wider proptech market, which means funding patterns here are influenced by investor sentiment that spans real estate technology more broadly rather than construction alone.

A decision-maker evaluating deployment should note that the clearest near-term return documented in this sector is in safety and preconstruction coordination, both areas with measurable cost outcomes and existing regulatory pressure that can justify the investment case. The technology vendor landscape is tracked through research networks and trade bodies rather than dominated by a single platform, which means integration with existing project management and BIM workflows is a practical first question. Adoption is rising but still below a majority of firms, so competitive differentiation through early deployment remains plausible, though the project-based nature of construction means firm-level adoption numbers can obscure significant variation in actual jobsite use.
